claim: ClusterTitleField can report its rename twice: Enter, then the blur from its own removal
`dragEdit`'s `depth` climbs a cluster loop forever, hanging the tab on a box drag
An edit that changes the errors while paused wipes the previews already drawn, and they stay blank until play

triage.scenario: previews on 'scope', play, pause: the last frame's scopes stay on the stages. Now edit a stage so it errors (or clear an error): `publishErrors` publishes `errorsRun(next)`, a run with no previews, so every scope on the chart disappears; `frame` only runs while playing, so nothing redraws them until the user plays again. Expected: an error change keeps the previews of the run it replaces (or redraws from the taps), so the frozen scopes stay up.
triage.cause: errors-only run replaces preview run

claim: clusterStages deletes a boxed cluster it empties, whereas moveToCluster keeps it

triage.scenario: under `nodeGraph`, cluster `P` has a `clusterBoxes` entry and holds only stage `A`; stage `B` is top level. `EffectEditorApi.cluster(['A', 'B'])` → the members have different parents, so `pruneClusters(clusters, taken)` runs with no `keep`, `P` is emptied and dropped, and `withClusters` drops its box too. Dragging `A` out of `P` instead goes through `moveToCluster`, whose `boxed` keep leaves `P` and its box in place. The same question, whether a boxed cluster survives being emptied, gets two answers. Taking members out for a new group should keep a boxed `P`, as a drag does.
triage.cause: pruneClusters called without the boxed keep

claim: `useFollowAudioRunner` never hands the runner a `sources` that went back to `undefined`
Node defs built for a structural batch the graph refuses are dropped without `dispose`
nextStageId mints an id a cluster already has, so adding a stage makes that cluster vanish

triage.scenario: a doc has a cluster whose id is `blur` (or `audio.gain`, any id equal to a stage type name; clusters from a loaded file can be named anything). `EffectEditorApi.addStage(blurType)` calls `nextStageId(d.pipeline, 'blur')`, which checks only `p.stages`, so the new stage gets id `blur`. Now a stage and a cluster share an id: `checkPipeline` reports `duplicate-cluster` ("has the id of a stage"), `uniqueClusters` drops the cluster from every look, and `editorScene.clusterOf` answers `undefined` for it, so the user's group disappears and can no longer be edited. It should have minted `blur-2`, as `nextClusterId` already does in the other direction by excluding stage ids.
triage.cause: id-taken set omits cluster ids

claim: `clusterAt` / `clusterSlotsAt` read a twice-named member's parent as the *last* cluster naming it; the rest of diagram uses the first
Remaking the live audio runner closes the bitmaps of the run still on screen before the new runner's state renders
A node `build` that throws freezes the whole live graph, with no stage named
A partially failed graph start leaves the healthy sources playing while the runner's state stays paused

triage.scenario: a pipeline with two sources, one of whose `start` throws (an `AudioGraph.start` contract case: "A source whose start throws is left stopped while the rest start, and the first error is rethrown"). `play()` calls `graph.start()`, which throws after starting the other sources, so `set({ playing: true })` never runs and the promise rejects. The graph is audibly playing, but `state.playing` is false: `useFollowAudioRunner` never starts its preview loop, a UI shows a Play button for sound already playing, and the failing stage gets no error in the run. It should publish `playing: true` (the graph is running) and report the failed stage under `errors`, as `applyStructure` does for a source that fails to start.
triage.cause: exception from a partial start skips the state update

claim: typeColors uses up a series color for every type that already has its own color, so later types get shifted colors

triage.scenario: the colors are `{ image: '#fff' }` and the ports, in order, are `image` then `number`. `colors.size` counts `image`, so `number` gets `series[1]` and `series[0]` is never used. With one given type per pipeline, the documented "next in `series`" order is shifted by one for every given color before it.
triage.cause: series index counts given colors

claim: applyStructure reports "nothing changed" after a runtime throw in a batch with no adds, though every patch landed
checkPipeline does not report two wires feeding an input that does not accept many

triage.scenario: a pipeline loaded from a file has wires a.out→b.in and c.out→b.in, where `b.in` has no `many`. The editor treats that input as already fed (`inputFed`/`canWire` in edit.ts refuse a second wire), and the runner reads only one value for a non-`many` input, but `checkPipeline` reports nothing, `drawableWires` draws neither wire as a problem, and `onProblems` says the pipeline is fine. The same question ("may this input take a second wire?") gets two different answers. checkPipeline should report the second wire (for example as a new `kind`) so the drawing flags it.
triage.cause: fan-in rule enforced only in the editor

claim: Renaming a cluster whose label has leading or trailing spaces records a 'Rename group' edit when nothing changed

triage.scenario: a doc loaded with cluster label `" Mix "` (docShape accepts any string). The user opens the rename field and presses Enter, or clicks away, without typing. `ClusterTitleField` hands back `text.trim()` = `"Mix"`, and `"Mix" !== " Mix "`, so `onChange` gets a doc and an undo entry for an edit the user never made. It should compare against the trimmed label, or not trim.
triage.cause: trimmed text compared to untrimmed label

claim: moveRunInChain picks a moved run's unwired main port without regard to type or control, refusing valid moves

triage.scenario: the stage being moved is the head of the main chain (`i === 0`, so `mainIn` has no entry for it), and its first open input is a control-typed port, for example inputs `[{ id: 'amount', type: 'number' }, { id: 'in', type: 'image' }]` with `number` marked `control`. Dragging it into the middle of the chain gives `sIn = pick(first, 'inputs')`, which is `'amount'`. The wire into it, a→first, reuses `wAB`'s data output (`aOut = p.wires[wAB].from.port`, an image port). `canWire` then sees `image` ≠ `number` and the move returns `null`, so the drop is refused even though `'in'` would take the wire. The same happens on the `sOut = pick(last, 'outputs')` side for a run whose last stage is the chain's tail and whose first output is control-typed. The code should pick a non-control port, or one matching the type of the neighbor it is being wired to (the `type` argument `pick` already accepts).
triage.cause: port pick ignores the neighbor's type and control wires

claim: Reordering lanes drops every laneOrder entry whose type has no stage yet

triage.scenario: doc.laneOrder is `['mask', 'image', 'number']` and the pipeline currently has no mask stage. `lanes` draws only used types (`laneTypes` keeps the `first` the pipeline uses), so the drawn lane order is image, number. Dragging number above image calls `setLaneOrder(doc, ['number', 'image'])`, erasing `mask`; adding a mask stage later puts its lane last instead of first. Expected: the move reorders the drawn lanes and keeps the undrawn entries of `doc.laneOrder` (and the options' `lanes`) where they were.
triage.cause: lane order rebuilt from drawn lanes only

claim: A missing numeric param plays at the factory's default, not the stage type's, while discrete settings use the stage type's
Reconnecting a wire under nodeGraph keeps its hand-set route, which a reorder's rewiring drops
EffectEditor's `renaming` state outlives the cluster it names, so a later cluster minted with the same id opens the rename field unasked
`pause()` (or `reset()`) during `play()`'s unlock is undone when the unlock resolves
A chain reorder refuses to wire into a `many` input that already has a side wire
Moving a cluster translates the routes of wires inside it but not their labels' `near` points
Recovering from a failed setter in a multi-parameter update re-applies the setters that already succeeded, so each runs twice
`typeColors` gives every type `undefined` as its color when the theme's `series` is empty
checkPipeline does not report a cluster that names the same member twice

triage.scenario: `clusters: [{ id: 'g', members: ['a', 'a'] }]`: the second `a` finds `holder.get('a') === 'g'` and the `first !== cluster.id` test skips it, so no problem is reported, though `duplicate-member` exists for a member held twice and the repeat reaches the looks and `dissolveCluster` (which then splices `a` into the parent twice). Expected: a `duplicate-member` problem for the repeat.
triage.cause: same-cluster repeat exempted

claim: clusterContents and clusterParents disagree with how clusters are drawn when a member is named twice or clusters loop

triage.scenario: stage `s` is listed in cluster A and again in cluster B (A first). `nestClusters` (packages/diagram/src/clusterTree.ts:48) draws `s` only in A. `clusterContents(doc, 'B')` still counts `s`, so dragging B's box under nodeGraph (`dragEdit` → `moveCluster`) also moves `s`, which is drawn inside A. `clusterRuns`/`clusterGripOf` read the same over-broad membership. For a loop (A holds B, B holds A), `nestClusters` drops B's claim on A, so A is drawn at the top level. `clusterParents` still records B as A's parent, so `clusterDepth` and `clusterSlotsAt`'s sibling set are computed against a tree the drawing does not have. Both inputs are ones `checkPipeline` reports but a doc can still hold, and the editor draws them. The rule for who holds what is decided once in `nestClusters`, and again, differently, here.
triage.cause: second definition of cluster membership diverges from nestClusters

claim: A wire repeating an earlier wire's id is edited through that id: deleting or reconnecting it changes both wires
The cluster reorder counts order items that have no drawn box as drawn, while the stage reorder drops them

triage.scenario: the stage reorder passes `drawnOrder(order, boxOf)` to `stageMove`, so only items with a drawn box count as "drawn" (the comment at `drawnOrder` says a move's indices count only these). `clusterReorder` passes the raw `order` to `clusterMove`, and `drawnOf(order)` there treats an item with no box as drawn. `dropInGap` then stops trying gaps at that stage, and `indices(before, true)` counts it. A look item without a box (one not yet laid out, or one the look leaves undrawn) can therefore make a cluster drop that the stage path would accept come back `null`, or land in a different gap. The two reorders read "drawn" differently.
triage.cause: drawnOrder filter not applied on the cluster path

claim: A structural batch the graph refuses blocks every param write in that sync and every later sync until the structure changes

triage.scenario: the graph refuses a structural patch during `graph.check`, for example a custom `AudioStageNode.build` that hands back a def already in use (`defInUse`). `landed` is then false, so `sets` is `[]` and `plan` stays `from`. Every later `setPipeline` re-diffs from that same `from`, rebuilds the same refused structure, and is refused again. While that persists, no level change to any other stage reaches the graph. If `failingStage` finds no quoted id in the message, no stage gets an error either, and the only sign is a `console.warn`. Sets on nodes that are unchanged in both plans could still be applied.
triage.cause: param writes gated on the whole structural batch landing

claim: canConnect counts an id-less or repeated-id wire as feeding its own input while its end is dragged

triage.scenario: doc has an id-less wire `src.out → gain.in` (or a second wire repeating an earlier wire's id), `gain.in` takes one wire. The user drags that wire's `from` end to another output. `except` is `built.wireOf(moving.edge)`, the id the wire gets in `ensureWireIds(doc)` (e.g. `w1`), but `fed` filters `now().doc.pipeline.wires` — the raw doc, where the wire's id is `undefined` (or the earlier wire's id). The filter keeps the moving wire, `inputFed` sees `gain.in` already fed, and `canConnect` refuses every target, so the reconnect can never be made. `onReconnect` itself runs on `ensureWireIds(d)` and would accept it; the two disagree on which wire is being moved. Should test against `ensureWireIds(doc).pipeline`.
triage.cause: raw doc ids compared with ensured ids

claim: A wire id equal to a stage id (or a minted id colliding across the wire and stage namespaces) makes diagramScene throw, and checkPipeline never reports the collision

triage.scenario: a doc with a stage whose id is `w1` (any user-chosen id) and no wires; the user connects two ports in `EffectEditor`. `addWire` → `nextWireId` checks only wire ids and mints `w1`. `wireEdges`/`drawableWires` keep the wire's id as the edge id, so the edge spec and the stage's node spec are both `w1`, and `diagramScene` throws "two things would share the scene id \"w1\"" (fromData.ts:249): the editor and `EffectChart` crash on the next render. The same happens for a loaded pipeline whose wire id equals a stage or cluster id, and `ensureWireIds` mints the same way. Likewise `nextStageId` avoids only stage ids: adding a stage whose type id equals an existing cluster id (a hand-written cluster `source`, then Add stage "source") makes `uniqueClusters` silently drop that cluster and its box. Expected: minted ids avoid every id sharing the scene's id space (stages, clusters, wires), and `checkPipeline` reports a wire id that names a stage or cluster, as it does a cluster id naming a stage.
triage.cause: id minting checks only its own namespace

claim: livePlan judges feedback loops over every raw wire, though it feeds stages only over wires the chart draws
Shipped audio nodes throw at build, not in `settings`, for a missing or unknown discrete setting
EffectEditorApi.cluster makes and reports a group of ids that name nothing
Two wires sharing an `id` make `EffectChart`/`EffectEditor` throw in render; nothing reports or drops the repeat
Two wires with the same ends map to one wire id, so editing the second edits the first
Live audio previews always land on port `out` regardless of the stage's actual output port name

triage.scenario: a caller passes its own `nodes` (`LiveAudioRunnerOptions.nodes`, `AudioStageNodes` keyed by any stage type) for a stage whose output port is `signal`, not `out`. While playing with previews on, every frame draws a bitmap into `stages[id].previews.out`. The look keeps its preview slot under `previewRowId('signal')`, so nothing ever shows in that slot. A new bitmap is still made every frame for a key nobody reads. The preview should go to the stage's shown port (its first output, as `shownPorts` gives).
triage.cause: port id hard-coded; previews never see the pipeline

claim: A numeric audio setting given as text is passed through unparsed, while a level given as text is parsed
A failing param write drops every later stage's param write, and the plan still records them as applied
A wire picked before a controlled `selected` change shows picked again once `selected` returns to null
A cluster id with the reserved `~` prefix is neither reported nor refused, and collides with look-made ids
Live audio runner draws every scope and spectrum at the default 48-unit size, ignoring the look's previewSize

triage.scenario: a chart or editor whose look sets `showPreviews: true, previewSize: { width: 160, height: 48 }` (or `96`) shows a live audio pipeline from `useLiveAudioRunner`. The slot is laid out at 160×48, but `draw` paints each tap at `PREVIEW_SIZE` × `PREVIEW_SIZE` (48×48 → 96×96 device px), so the bitmap is stretched: a wide slot gets a distorted waveform, and a larger square slot gets a blurry one. The image runner takes the same setting as an option (`runner/pass.ts:23`, `useEffectRunner`'s `previewSize`). `LiveAudioRunnerOptions`/`UseLiveAudioRunnerOptions` have no matching field, so the option is dropped on this path.
triage.cause: preview size hard-coded; no option threaded through

claim: A replaced runner's last preview bitmaps can be closed while a render still shows them
`sync` assumes a throwing structural apply changed nothing, but `graph.apply` keeps applying after an execution-time failure
The live audio plan plays wires the looks do not draw: a wire from a missing or input port, or into a missing port of the output
Reorder moves index the unfiltered `order.items` while the slots were built from the boxed subset
Clearing a route that does not exist still sends an 'Edit route' edit under nodeGraph

triage.scenario: under `nodeGraph`, a wire with no entry in `doc.routes` reports a `RouteChange` with empty `waypoints`. `setWireRoute(d, id, [])` returns a new doc with `routes: {}`, and `commit` hands it to `onChange` as 'Edit route': an undo entry that changes nothing, and an empty `routes` written into the doc. The rack/lanes branch just above returns `null` for the same case (`was === undefined`), so each look answers it differently.
triage.cause: no no-op check on the nodeGraph path

claim: A live runner's apply-time failures are shown once, then erased by the next unrelated edit while the stage stays broken
A wire minted into a freed id by a chain move inherits the removed wire's label placement
Editor connect/reconnect refuses rack's tap ports: port ids are not untapped as the edge mapping does
A delay node's maximum delay time is fixed when it is built, so a time later raised as a level past that maximum is not honored

triage.scenario: `time` is a level, so editing it sends a `set` patch and never a rebuild. `createDelayNode` fixes `maxTime = max(2000, time)` when it is built. Built at 300 ms and then set to 5000 ms, the live graph clamps the delay at 2000 ms. After `reset`, or any rebuild of that node, the same pipeline plays a 5000 ms delay. One pipeline plays two ways depending on how it got there.
triage.cause: build-time max for a live level

claim: A numeric audio param without a `control` plays at its default, while a setting without one is used as written
One wire into a port the node lacks rolls the live graph back whole: no other edit reaches it
EffectEditorApi.dissolveCluster does not pin shown stages under nodeGraph, unlike cluster
The live audio graph keeps a level the plan stopped giving, where a fresh build uses the node's default
A bypassed stage whose ports are not typed `audio` cuts the signal instead of passing it through

triage.scenario: with custom `nodes`, a stage type whose ports are typed something else (e.g. `signal`) sits mid-chain and has `bypassed: true`. `firstAudio` is `undefined`, so `fed` keeps only wires where `w.to.port === undefined`, which is none. The stage has inputs and nothing fed, so the plan `continue`s without setting `origins`. Everything downstream then has no origin and is left out, so bypassing the stage silences the chain. It should carry its first input through. `played` itself never checks port types, so these stages otherwise play normally.
triage.cause: bypass pass-through keyed to the literal port type 'audio'
